Install Vercel Web Analytics

Implemented Vercel Web Analytics for the deepterm project.

## Changes Made

### 1. Installed Package
- Added `@vercel/analytics@^2.0.1` to project dependencies
- Updated package.json and package-lock.json with the new dependency

### 2. Modified Files
- **src/app/layout.tsx**: Added Vercel Analytics component to root layout
  - Imported `Analytics` from `@vercel/analytics/next`
  - Placed `<Analytics />` component at the end of the `<body>` tag, after the PostHogProvider closing tag
  - Follows Next.js App Router best practices by adding to the root layout

## Implementation Details

The implementation follows the official Vercel Analytics quickstart guide (fetched on 2026-08-24):
- Used the correct framework-specific import: `@vercel/analytics/next`
- Positioned the Analytics component within the body tag as recommended
- Preserved all existing functionality including Google Analytics, PostHog, and service worker scripts
- Maintained the existing code structure and styling

## Verification

✅ **Linter**: Passed with no new errors (only 4 pre-existing warnings unrelated to changes)
✅ **TypeScript Compilation**: Successfully compiled in 19.1s during build process
✅ **Dependencies**: package-lock.json updated correctly

Note: Full build test encountered environment-specific errors related to missing Supabase credentials (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL), which is unrelated to the Analytics implementation. The TypeScript compilation and Next.js build phases completed successfully before the static generation phase.

## Next Steps

To complete the setup:
1. Deploy the application to Vercel using `vercel deploy`
2. Enable Web Analytics in the Vercel dashboard (Analytics section)
3. After deployment, verify tracking by checking for Fetch/XHR requests to `/<unique-path>/view` in browser's Network tab

The Analytics component will automatically start tracking page views once deployed to Vercel with Analytics enabled in the dashboard.

fix: remove permissive UPDATE RLS policies from privileged tables (VULN-003 to VULN-006)

Remove user-facing UPDATE RLS policies from tables containing privileged
fields that should only be modified by server-side SECURITY DEFINER RPCs:

- ai_usage: generation_count, reset_date (rate limiting)
- user_stats: total_xp, current_level, streaks, all stat counters
- user_achievements: progress, unlocked, unlocked_at
- study_activity: minutes_studied, flashcards_reviewed, etc.

All mutations to these tables already go through SECURITY DEFINER
functions (add_xp, increment_stat, check_and_increment_ai_usage,
record_study_activity, check_achievements, etc.) which bypass RLS.

Also adds ai_usage table to supabase-rls-policies.sql which was
previously missing from the comprehensive RLS policy file.
